videos.caption: pricing my work is truly my LEAST favourite thing 😭  especially after trying to look closer at the numbers behind my small ceramic business. i’m trying to map out the potential 1, 3, and 5 year revenue and expense projections to see if investing in a kiln and building this business actually makes any sense. at my current $30-$65 price point, i’m losing money selling my work and cannot justify a kiln. i’ve made the terrifying decision to raise my prices by 25-30%. the money will go towards expanding production (investing. in a kiln & shelving), upgrading my website, expanding to ship to the US, and finally, offering private lessons and workshops.  with the price increase, I will still need to survive 6 months - 1 year without a livable wage / making profit. i’ll be focusing on my higher-margin petal bowls and bring in some more affordable $25 products like spoon rests and trinket dishes to keep things as accessible as possible. my mugs are not viable as they take me 2hrs each, but i’m going to keep making them for now and hope i can speed it up. no more lidded jars outside of speciality collections as the margins are too low.  i’m also going to try to secure 1-2 freelance social media clients to provide me with some supplement income as a buffer. this is the behind the scenes of small ceramics business’ that you normally don’t see, because it’s not nearly as cute or fun as the pots themselves. #potterybusiness #ceramics #smallbusiness #priceincrease #handmadeceramics

Here are the results of the “new” renditions of a batch of jars I haven’t made any of since about 2014. I both like them more than I thought I would and also feel slightly disconnected from them as they no longer really feel as if they fit my overall style of work, but they are neat objects, the lids fit wonderfully and they were a pleasure to create. If you’d like to watch a much longer narrated film that explains each step in the crafting process in great detail, that’s the subject of my YouTube video this weekend, (a link to which you can find via the Linktree in my profile biography).   They’re a lot more graft that’s for sure. In making a lid with a thrown knob there’s much more double-checking to see if it fits, lots more faffing and back-and-forth. In a way, the style I’ve settled on, which you see more commonly in my work, makes for a more fluid process as the lid can be trimmed in-situ atop the pot and it can also be used functionally like a check in order to trim the jar’s body. You can’t do either of those with these smaller lids that sit within a gallery within the jar, thus you have to work slower and more carefully.   I’ve definitely got some changes I’ll make when I next make a batch and they’re mostly to do with the knob itself. In all of these iterations they feel ever so slightly off. They aren’t tall or narrow enough to match the finesse of the rest of my ceramics and I think that’s where I feel the most unsure about these. Lids like this simply feel more traditional, there’s a conventional element that my larger, more prominent lids don’t have.   Either way, you’ll have to let me know what you think, and if you’d like to hear me explain all the moments quickly skipped over in this short video in much more detail, I recommend watching the 40-minute film over on my YouTube channel.   Thanks for watching!   #pottery #satisfying #jar #handmade #craft

easy bowls in just a few steps I normally hand carve but I wanted to make a bunch of bowls for a market that’s coming up and this allowed me to do it quicker. I have the right roller handle but for some reason this specific roller doesn’t fit so i’m using my calipers 💁🏻‍♀️ Things to note: when rolling a texture roller on the wheel make sure you leave a good thickness. This is probably more than a 1/4 inch.  Right before I use the roller I dip it in clean water and shake off the excess. Don’t let it sit in water. it will get too swollen to fit in your handle.  A lot of this video is sped up. Rolling the texture and shaping is done at a medium slow speed. You’ll have to adjust based on your usage.  You don’t have to use this specific rib. i’ve even used cd’s before. #pottery #ceramics #ceramica #funny

Here’s a completed apothecary jar and a full overview of how it’s made. For this type of lidded jar, the base and lid are thrown from one continuous piece of clay, then cut open and trimmed to create the inner edges and gallery so the lid doesn’t slide off. I like this type of piece because it has a continuous line from the base to the top of the knob. It’s a very elegant shape and one I imagine would look lovely on a shelf holding trinkets, spices, or chocolates. #pottery #studioceramics #wheelthrown #handmade #potteryartist
